Appearance:
 Shri Ashok Kumar Agrawal - learned Counsel for appellant  Company.

ORDER The present Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred by the appellant- Insurance Company under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, calling in question the Award dated 04.07.2025 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Karera, District Shivpuri, in MACC No.16 of 2024,
whereby compensation of Rs. 5,05,340/- has been awarded in favour of the claimants, who are the parents of deceased baby Jhanvi, aged about 9 months.
2. Brief facts of the case reveal that on 22.11.2023 the deceased child Jhanvi was playing outside her house when the driver of a loading vehicle bearing registration No. MP-33-G-1694, by driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, hit the child, resulting in grievous injuries.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Karera, District Shivpuri
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The child succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
Thereafter, the parents of the deceased filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act before the Claims Tribunal.

3. The Claims Tribunal, after appreciating the oral and documentary evidence available on record,
including the statements of the parents of the deceased child, recorded a finding that the accident occurred solely due to rash and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:104 2 MA-8069-2025 negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
The Tribunal held the driver, owner and insurer jointly and severally liable and consequently awarded compensation of Rs. 5,05,340/- in favour of the claimants.

1 4.
Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company assailed the impugned Award on the ground that it is contrary to law and facts on record.
It was contended that the Tribunal committed an error in assessing the notional income of the deceased child at Rs. 20,000/- per annum and in granting addition towards future prospects.
It was further argued that in the case of death of an infant child, neither income nor future prospects could be legally attributed.
Objection was also raised to the application of multiplier 20, contending that it has resulted in excessive compensation.
According to the appellant, the claimants cannot be treated as dependents of a 9-month-old child and, therefore, the grant of compensation under the head of loss of dependency is unsustainable.
On these grounds, reduction of compensation and setting aside of the impugned Award was prayed for.

5. Considered the submissions advanced on behalf of the appellant and perused the entire record.
Upon such consideration, this Court finds no substance in the contentions raised.
6.
It is a settled principle of law that in cases involving death of a minor child, compensation cannot be determined by applying a rigid formula based solely on actual income or dependency.

The assessment of compensation in such cases has to be made on the touchstone of just, fair and reasonable compensation, keeping in view the loss of future prospects, expectancy of life and the irreparable loss suffered by the parents.

The notional income assessed by the Tribunal and the application of multiplier, keeping in view the age of the parents, are in accordance with the settled principles governing assessment of compensation under the Motor NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:104 3 MA-8069-2025 Vehicles Act.

2026:MPHC-GWL:104 3 MA-8069-2025 Vehicles Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 7. The contention that future prospects cannot be considered in the case of a child is misconceived.

The law recognizes that some degree of enhancement is permissible to arrive at just compensation,
particularly where the Tribunal has exercised its discretion in a judicious and reasonable manner.

No perversity, arbitrariness or illegality has been pointed out in the reasoning adopted by the Claims Tribunal.
8.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal cannot be said to be excessive or unjust.
On the contrary, it fulfills the mandate of Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act, which requires the Tribunal to award compensation which appears to be just.
The scope of interference in appellate jurisdiction under Section 173 of the Act is limited, and in the absence of any material irregularity or legal infirmity, no interference is warranted.
9. Consequently, the Miscellaneous Appeal filed by the appellant-Insurance Company is dismissed.
The Award dated 04.07.2025 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Karera, District Shivpuri, in MACC No.16 of 2024 is hereby affirmed.
No order as to costs.
